newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas to execute three people on same day.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas to execute three people on same day.

text.p: Appeals failed on Tuesday for three condemed men and all three were scheduled to die on Wednesday, the second triple execution in the United States since the death penalty was restored in 1974.
The first triple execution, in 1994, was also carried out in Arkansas.

Paul Ruiz, 49, and Earl Denton, 47, were convicted of killing two Arkansas policemen in 1977. The Arkansas Supreme Court struck down their first conviction in 1978, citing pre-trial publicity. The two were convicted again in a second trial, and were again given the death sentence.

Ruiz and Denton escaped from an Oklahoma prison work detail before the Arkansas killings. Although they were convicted only of the deaths of the policemen, authorities in Texas and Louisiana say they provided evidence following their capture that implicated them in seven other killings.
The third man scheduled for death Wednesday night is Kirt W. Wainwright, 30, sentenced to die for the 1988 murder of an Arkansas retail clerk.
"I want to see him die. I want to watch it. I want him to beg for his life like my mother did," said Angela Smith Cunningham, a daughter of the victim, Barbara Smith.
A state judge Tuesday rejected arguments by all three inmates that they had insufficient time to prepare for a clemency hearing.
Later Tuesday, a federal district judge rejected Wainwright's arguments.
All three men have last-minute appeals pending with the Supreme Court, but they are not expected to be successful.
